title: Playing today and Frank's bass
summary: Frank says he plays little now apart from Godfrey and talks about instruments and cellist Bernie.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now, these bands today, I don't play with anybody now, except Godfrey once in a while. You don't play with me that much. I don't want no fucking-
I don't want no frassling jobs.
No, neither do I. Thank you. I had- I got stuck like that.

I played the other night. I moved on to- You know, you can tell him. The other night I moved that damn instrument outside, I said I was ready to fall to pieces. That's right. And I didn't work hard, because, I mean, it was not a hard job.

Well, he stuck with me. If I don't- If I don't help him get his instrument, he can't go to a job. So, by the time he booked a job, he got to put a bass on. Put the bass on top of the barbara hub. Incidentally, that bass, I told my sister, I said, you didn't like bass fiddles around the house at all. Oh, this symphony boy there last night asked me, he says, if you ever have any instruments, he says, I'd like to buy them. I'd like to buy them. I told him, I says, in my mind, I said to myself, he ain't getting paid, and he's talking about buying instruments over there. Now, I started telling him about Bernie's cello. Bernie told me, he says, that's a $12,000 cello. He says, it's registered. I says, where in the hell are you going to get a cello player that can give you $12,000? I said, for God's sake. I said, that's a starvation instrument to start off with. Who is Bernie? Bernie Richter. He's a cello player, the biggest hustler that's ever hit the city of New Orleans. Oh, yeah. He drove a cab in New York, played some of those off-night shows and stuff.
